body:
I can confirm this on Chromium 152 (Linux) since 4.4.dev4. It shows as 200% CPU usage in the task manager on a Ryzen 9 9950X3D. 4.4.dev3 and prior are "unaffected" in the sense that CPU usage is only stuck to 100% with them, instead of 200%.

Currently bisecting the issue.

<details>
<summary> An issue with compiling old versions I managed to work around</summary>

I'm trying to bisect but haven't managed to build the 4.4.dev4 web editor because of an Emscripten build error:

```
$ scons -j32 scu_build=all platform=web target=editor debug_symbols=no
scons: Reading SConscript files ...

scons: Building targets ...

[100%] em++: warning: -pthread + ALLOW_MEMORY_GROWTH may run non-wasm code slowly, see https://github.com/WebAssembly/design/issues/1271 [-Wpthreads-mem-growth]
```

I've installed Emscripten 3.1.68 for the purpose of compiling these old versions, which should suffice as per the [4.4 branch documentation](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.4/engine_details/development/compiling/compiling_for_web.html). Any ideas?
</details>

> [!NOTE]
>
> During bisecting, at some commits, the build system tries to install a service worker file that doesn't exist anywhere in the codebase. I've removed references to it in `platform/web/emscripten_helpers.py`. That seemed to do the trick, as we don't need the service worker for local testing as long as we use `platform/web/serve.py` to set cross-origin isolation headers.

cc @Faless

> I'm trying to bisect but haven't managed to build the 4.4.dev4 web editor because of an Emscripten build error:

I assume `4.4.dev4` was still using the emcc from the [4.3 branch](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.3/contributing/development/compiling/compiling_for_web.html#doc-compiling-for-web), i.e. `3.1.39`.

I bisected the regression to https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/38208. This likely occurs because the Dummy audio driver endlessly spins on the Web platform.

We should probably fix this, but as a hotfix, we could choose to keep the standard audio driver on the Web platform while in the project manager. Browsers seem to intelligently figure out whether a tab is actually playing audio before showing the "playing audio" icon on the tab that lets the user mute the tab.
